$comment: Drive/walk routing: A* over the committed OSM graph, then the ML chain prices it.
image_prompt: Draw a clean UML sequence diagram with four participants: 'Android app', 'FastAPI', 'routing.py (A* over city_graph)', 'models.py (ML)'. Number every message. Show the app sending pickup and drop-off lat/lon, the routing module snapping both points to the nearest graph nodes, running A*, then running A* again twice more with already-used roads penalised to produce alternative routes, then the ML module converting distance into an ETA and a fare, and finally a dashed response returning a polyline plus turn-by-turn steps. Add a labelled loop fragment around the alternative-route calls marked 'loop: up to 3 distinct routes'.

style.look: clean UML-style sequence diagram, flat modern, generous vertical spacing
conventions: Participants across the top as labelled boxes with vertical dashed lifelines.
Solid arrow = request. Dashed arrow = response.
Self-call drawn as a small loop back onto the same lifeline.
Number every message so the reading order is unambiguous.
Draw alt / opt fragments as a labelled rectangle spanning the lifelines involved.

messages.label: pick graph: drive -> city_graph.json, walk -> walk_graph.json (falls back to drive if missing)
snap origin and destination to nearest graph nodes
A* with haversine heuristic -> best path
re-run A* with previous roads costing 2.4x -> a genuinely different route
build polyline, count turns, derive turn-by-turn steps from bearing changes
up to 3 routes: polyline_latlon, distance_km, turns, steps
200 primary route + alternatives, each with eta_min and fare_usd

fragments.label: up to 3 distinct routes
fragments.note: each iteration penalises every edge used by the routes found so far, so the search is pushed onto different streets

fragments.label: walk mode
fragments.note: walking skips the fare model entirely: eta = distance / 4.8 km/h and fare_usd is 0

annotations: This path never touches the network - both graphs are baked into the container image.
Contrast with /transit: this answer does not depend on what time you ask.
